title: The radial retraction onto a closed ball is 1-Lipschitz
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and ρ ∈ ℝ with ρ > 0, and give ℝ^P = Euclid P the Euclidean norm. Then there is a map r : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that (1) r is 1-Lipschitz, i.e. ‖r(x) − r(y)‖ ≤ ‖x − y‖ for all x, y (LipschitzWith 1 r); (2) ‖r(y)‖ ≤ ρ for every y ∈ ℝ^P; (3) r(y) = y for every y with ‖y‖ ≤ ρ. (For example the nearest-point retraction r(y) = y for ‖y‖ ≤ ρ and r(y) = (ρ/‖y‖)·y otherwise.)
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∃ r : Euclid P → Euclid P, LipschitzWith 1 r ∧ (∀ y, ‖r y‖ ≤ ρ) ∧ ∀ y, ‖y‖ ≤ ρ → r y = y
